findings.recommendation: Confirm the on-premises VPN device / service is running and reachable on UDP 500/4500, shared key and IKE/IPsec parameters match, then review IKEDiagnosticLog / TunnelDiagnosticLog for the disconnect reason.
findings.remediation_script:
# Human review required. Read-only verification (the agent never runs writes):
az network vpn-connection show -g rg-netops-hub -n cn-hub-to-onprem --query "{status:connectionStatus,tunnels:tunnelConnectionStatus}"
# KQL: AzureDiagnostics | where Category in ("TunnelDiagnosticLog","IKEDiagnosticLog")
findings.title: IPsec connection cn-hub-to-onprem is NotConnected

findings.recommendation: BGP runs over the IPsec tunnel: fix the tunnel first, then verify peer IP / ASN on both sides and that the on-premises BGP speaker is running.
findings.remediation_script:
# Human review required. Read-only verification (the agent never runs writes):
az network vnet-gateway list-bgp-peer-status -g rg-netops-hub -n vpngw-hub -o table
findings.title: BGP peer 10.100.0.4 on vpngw-hub is Connecting

findings.recommendation: Disconnect on one instance followed by connect on the other is failover/maintenance; repeated disconnect/reconnect on the same instance points to DPD, packet loss or the on-premises device. Correlate with GatewayDiagnosticLog and IKEDiagnosticLog.
findings.remediation_script:
# Human review required. Read-only verification (the agent never runs writes):
# KQL (Log Analytics):
AzureDiagnostics | where Category == "TunnelDiagnosticLog" | where remoteIP_s == "20.50.0.10" | project TimeGenerated, OperationName, instance_s, remoteIP_s | order by TimeGenerated asc
findings.title: Tunnel to 20.50.0.10 on vpngw-hub: 2 disconnect(s) and still down
